mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) reflects stronger economic demand, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7.5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If UNRATE exceeds 7.5% but SPX 20-day returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7%, it indicates a sluggish economic recovery, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 30% of cases, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during an early-cycle recovery signals improving consumer confidence and demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5% YoY but SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects stronger supply chains and manufacturing activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% annualized signals rising inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as real earnings decline.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% but SPX 20-day returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases but retail sales (RSAFS) decline, it signals a mismatch in labor market strength and consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 30% of cases, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs increase and corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.
